subject: GGIR seems to ignore Timestamps while performing analysis on actigraph data

messages.author: cf90f22a7eee9265
messages.subject: GGIR seems to ignore Timestamps while performing analysis on actigraph data
parts:
Dear all, 
while analysis of accelerometric data is not my main field of research, colleagues asked me for help analyzing data of 2500 participants and they wanted to use the GGIR R-package. I did some testings with data from a smaller study and everything worked fine. Now I just got some real data from the bigger cohort study and they had the Idle Sleep Mode for the Actigraph device activated. As a result we got Raw data csv files with different lengths and leaps in time between them. Is there any way to take this into account using GGIR? At the moment it seems like R is ignoring the timestamps and uses just the 3 movement axis. I added the QC pdf to illustrate the problem. I hope anyone can help us to solve this problem. 

Best regards 

Dominic Bläsing

parts:
Hi Dominic,

Currently GGIR makes no attempt to facilitate ActiGraph's sleep.mode status. However, I am happy to implement such functionality as part of a paid consultancy. If you or anyone else is interested in hiring me to do this then send me a personal message. Alternatively, if you are familiar with software development: I welcome GitHub pull requests.

On a related note - As long as there is no reproducible description of the sleep.mode mechanism of ActiGraph, I would advise against using it because it represents a gap in the description of your research methods, which is not good for transparency and interpretation.

Best regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/
